rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Chapter asks whether Prince Rupert will gain honor in the wars or defeat the Earl of Essex and what will happen to him.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Composite outcome is not one unambiguous yes/no question.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: One target is whether Rupert wins public military honor.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Honor is different from battlefield victory, survival or confinement.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: A different target asks whether Rupert will overcome the Earl of Essex.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Opponent's military success is a separate endpoint.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The final component asks about Rupert's future fate.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Contains imprisonment and personal survival claims not equivalent to military honor.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The original polygonal horoscope prints 28 November 1642, at 9:23 AM.
rows.original_source_qualifications: The old historical time/calendar has not been independently recast.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says this particular question is not governed simply by standard vulgar rules.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Retrospective interpretive flexibility is a major test limitation.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He argues the astrologer should use special judgment rather than mechanically follow Guido or Haly.
rows.original_source_qualifications: No prospectively frozen unique method or scoring weights.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The unidentified questioner is characterized as a strong Parliament supporter.
rows.original_source_qualifications: His political interest may affect question interpretation and selection.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: involved himself and Fortune amongst us
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says the querent had his own person and fortune invested in the cause.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Source-side identification only; no independent name or file.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The ascendant and first-house lord signify the questioner.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Not a first-house assignment to Rupert.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Rupert as a noble and eminent man is assigned the tenth house and ruler.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Derived hierarchy is context-specific; no independent recalculation.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The tenth-house sign is Scorpio and its ruler is Mars in Lilly's judgment.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Printed planetary and sign claims not independently ephemeris-verified.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The Moon is placed in Cancer in the original reading.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Period dignity/aspect conventions not modern-recast.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly invokes the Moon's sinister trine to the tenth-house cusp.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Direction of trine and house cusp are important qualifiers.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: His initial interpretation was that Rupert's person faced little danger.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Source-side tentative judgment, not a separately confirmed life outcome.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: vulgar people and better quality honour
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He initially thought many common and higher-status people would honor Rupert.
rows.original_source_qualifications: This positive impression contrasts Lilly's later no-honor forecast.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly initially anticipated social respect for Rupert.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Qualitative social endpoint without defined measure.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He expected Rupert to take special care of his own person.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Behavioral forecast not independently observed.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He additionally sees Jupiter casting a dexter trine to tenth cusp.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Different planet and trine direction from Moon.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: we should not destroy his person
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He concluded Rupert would not be killed by parliamentary forces.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Negative death prediction must remain distinct from honor and capture.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly reports spending twenty-four hours deliberating on this question.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Method adaptation/deliberation may have included outside contextual knowledge; no preregistration.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: His later settled conclusion differs from the initial favorable social impression.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Both phases must be preserved; do not back-project final view as original instantaneous answer.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: gain no honour by this War
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He eventually predicts Rupert will gain no honor from this war.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Subjectively broad prediction, not a measured battlefield endpoint.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Neither luminary is said to be in the tenth house.
rows.original_source_qualifications: One astrological premise for no-honor conclusion.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Neither luminary supposedly makes a perfect aspect to Rupert's significator Mars.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Do not turn absence of this specific relation into absence of all good aspects.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: fall hatred and malice of all or many
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He predicts Rupert will become widely hated.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Populace and threshold 'all or many' highly flexible.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly attributes future hatred to Rupert's stubbornness and folly.
rows.original_source_qualifications: An authorial moral characterization, not independently verified personality diagnosis.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He forecasts Rupert ultimately departing without honor, love or friendship.
rows.original_source_qualifications: This is departure/status outcome, not death.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The final conclusion reiterates that Rupert would survive.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Repeated source forecast must not be counted as a second independent prediction.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Mars as ruler of Rupert's tenth is in detriment.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Essential dignity assertion not independently recalculated.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly interprets detriment as a corrupted fancy or judgment.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Period evaluative language, not clinical evidence.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The relevant significator is placed in a fixed sign.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Distinct from being in detriment.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly infers obstinacy, conceit and persistence in mistaken judgment.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Not a blinded trait measure.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He generalizes a war rule about an unfortunate Mars significator.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Not a calibrated military forecast model.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Support from the luminaries is lacking in the scenario.
rows.original_source_qualifications: An extra prerequisite, not unconditional all-Mars failure.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He allows that a party can survive under these adverse conditions.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Survival is different from victory or honor.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He expects no glorious military accomplishment even if the party survives.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Outcome must be recorded separately from life preservation.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: If he should worst Earle of Essex
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: A separate subsection directly considers Rupert defeating Essex.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Not the same as the initial general honor forecast.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Essex is signified by Venus as ruler of Taurus opposite Rupert's Scorpio tenth.
rows.original_source_qualifications: House derivation contextual to this two-party question.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly describes Venus in Aquarius.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Original glyph and positioning may need independent recalculation.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Venus is in Saturn's terms or bounds.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Separate essential dignity factor.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Saturn is also the ruler of the querent's ascendant.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Essex/Venus and querent/Saturn distinction.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Venus and Saturn are said to receive one another by exaltation/joy and terms.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Exact reception terms preserved without inferred historical cause.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon transfers Jupiter to Saturn trine
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The Moon transfers Jupiter's influence to Saturn by a strong trine in Lilly's judgment.
rows.original_source_qualifications: His asserted light-translation is unverified astronomical calculation.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Venus is described as separated from a square to Mars.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Past separating aspect rather than future application.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He infers a prior fight between Essex and Rupert.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Battle already occurred before the question; this is NOT a prospective forecast.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly connects this with the Battle of Edgehill occurring more than a month earlier.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Independently check dates and significance; no result is proven by this retroactive identification.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He claims Essex had the better of the Edgehill engagement.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Contested historical battle outcome; do not convert to an undisputed victory.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly bases that opinion partly on Essex holding ground when King and Rupert left.
rows.original_source_qualifications: One specific tactical metric, not a full victory judgment.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He alleges that many of the King's own officers agreed with his characterization.
rows.original_source_qualifications: No independent signed or dated testimony is provided in the chapter.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly writes that he positively affirmed Rupert would never prevail against Essex.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Predicted comparison requires defined battles and horizon; text is retrospective publication.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He asserts that Rupert did not prevail over Essex.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Self-reported outcome; not an independent predictive hit.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He claims to write as an expert for posterity.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Author's confidence is not external validation.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He frames his account for historical judgment by later generations.
rows.original_source_qualifications: No documented contemporaneous forecast freezing date.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The text shifts to a separate question about Rupert's later fate.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Different from honor or beating Essex.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Rupert's significator Mars is called peregrine.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Contextual period dignity judgment.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Mars is placed in the third house.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Different house from Rupert originally signified by tenth.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says he predicted Parliament would eventually have Rupert in its own custody and power.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Literal custody/control claim; not validated merely by later negotiations.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: do what we list with him
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He portrays Parliament as able to decide Rupert's fate at will.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Stronger prediction than being geographically nearby.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: His stated rationale is that Venus/Essex disposes of Mars/Rupert.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Astrological metaphor, not a causal military explanation.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: an errour in part I confesse
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly explicitly admits an error in part of his Rupert custody prediction.
rows.original_source_qualifications: This is a material negative, must not be laundered into a success.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He calls his forecast 'very near truth' despite the admission of error.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Authorial retrospective repair, not exact validated accuracy.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He recounts Rupert being besieged at Oxford in 1646.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Specific independent-history target not yet independently audited here.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says Rupert went to Oatlands after the surrender of Oxford.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Narrative details and sequence require independent records.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He asserts Rupert's movement violated an agreement or covenant.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Political allegation not independently corroborated here.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He says Rupert was at Parliament's mercy or could be judged by it.
rows.original_source_qualifications: This is an interpretive condition, not evidence of literal captive control.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He reports Parliament released/allowed Rupert to depart instead of retaining him.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Directly contradicts the strongest literal 'do what we list' custody outcome as asserted.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says Rupert ultimately escaped that fate.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Must be retained as explicit noncaptivity outcome.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: general fate Kingdom overcame private opinion
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He says national events overrode his individual astrological prediction.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Explicit statement that the forecast did not unfold as first expected.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He expresses relief Rupert escaped and describes him as capable but unfortunate.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Editorial sympathy after report, not predictive evidence.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The next chapter asks if royal forces from Ireland would harm Parliament and whether the Queen's army would advance/prosper.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Following topic opens PDF489, not LXXXV body.
